walls.min_wall.measured_on: one printer with a 0.6 nozzle: the starting value of the print-design skill; one project raised it to 2.0 for PETG by owner decision
walls.min_wall.description: least material between two faces of a printed part, for any role; a project sets its own value per target material

walls.min_wall_effective.measured_on: computed from the minimum wall and the line width of the declared target
walls.min_wall_effective.description: the wall limit a part is judged against: the minimum wall, and never under two lines of the target project

walls.slit_min.measured_on: decided: a narrower air gap is closed or bridged by the slicer; not measured
walls.slit_min.description: least width of an air gap between two walls of one part

walls.coverage_min.description: share of the surface the wall probe must have sampled; below it the result is "not proven", never a pass

walls.min_face_width.measured_on: one printer with a 0.6 nozzle: the starting value of the print-design skill
walls.min_face_width.description: a planar face narrower than this is a sliver, a ledge or the crescent of an old hole

walls.strip_turn_max.measured_on: decided, nobody measured it: a chamfer turns by 45 deg at each long side, one flat of a faceted tooth profile by 5 to 50, a ledge or a crescent by 90
walls.strip_turn_max.description: a narrow face is one flat of a chamfer, a bevel or a faceted curve, and no sliver, when each of its long sides turns by at most this angle and the sides that turn by more than half of it turn the same way

walls.load_path_min.measured_on: owner decision of one project for PETG (one printer, 0.6 nozzle); not measured
walls.load_path_min.description: least wall in a load path

walls.structural_target.measured_on: owner decision of one project for load-carrying links, where space exists; a target, not a floor
walls.structural_target.description: wall a load-carrying part is grown to where the space exists

walls.min_layers.measured_on: one printer: a one-layer cap was too weak on a print; 4 layers (0.8 mm) were used after it
walls.min_layers.description: least number of layers of a thin horizontal sheet (a cap over a pocket, a printed washer or shim)

walls.min_step.measured_on: in use in one project; where it comes from is not recorded
walls.min_step.description: a step between two faces lower than this is a modelling leftover, not a feature

walls.leftover_depth.measured_on: decided after six dents 0.2 mm deep stayed visible on a printed face
walls.leftover_depth.description: a dent, seam or pocket shallower than this has no function and is a leftover

rules.title: No wall thinner than the minimum
rules.statement: No wall, strap or neck of the exported STL is thinner than {walls.min_wall_effective}: the larger of {walls.min_wall} and two lines of the target project (one line is {target.line_width}). It is measured as material between faces on the STL. A wall under one line does not print at all. Rims round pockets, reliefs and holes count: no hit is hidden for being small. A neck is always an error. A thin sheet is fixed, or is a named exception with its reason and load case. A result that sampled less than {walls.coverage_min} of the surface is not proven and is not a pass.
rules.why: A 0.86 mm neck under a loaded hook passed the face-width check, which measured the wrong thing; the part was exported and stood on a plate. The older STL check hid small rims unless asked: the 0.95 mm rim beside an insert relief that later bulged is exactly such a hit. It also ran at its own default, below the wall the project had decided. A 0.95 mm tube wall and a 1.02 mm sheet stayed open with no waiver.
fix_order: Make the wall thicker: grow it into the free space, up to the real neighbour.
Move or shrink the feature that thins it: the hole, pocket, relief or notch.
Remove a thin feature that has no function.
A thin sheet that must stay (a shim, a bridge layer): owner waiver with the reason and the load case. A neck gets no waiver without a load case.
Not proven: run the wall check again with a longer budget; a partial result exports nothing.
rules.note: The older voxel tool (tools/bambu/wall_thickness.py) lists sheets under 2 mm3 only with --all and runs at its own --min: a clean run of it is not a pass of this rule.

rules.title: No air gap the slicer will close
rules.statement: No air gap between two walls of the STL is narrower than {walls.slit_min}: the slicer closes or bridges it. A slit that has to open or close in use (a clamp slit) is far wider, never under one line of the target project, and is looked at in the sliced path.
rules.why: A slit that was meant to let a clamp close was bridged in the print: the clamp could not close and the part was sawn.
fix_order: Widen the gap to a width the slicer keeps open.
Remove the gap: join the two walls.
A gap that must stay this narrow: owner waiver, after a look at the sliced path.

rules.title: A wall between one and two lines is a decision
rules.statement: A wall between one and two line widths of the target project (one line is {target.line_width}) is a decision, not a default. Classic walls lay two full lines into it and the bore inside closes. It prints only with a thin-wall generator (Arachne) set on that object and checked in the sliced path, and its size comes from a printed fit ladder, not from the model: a one-line tube prints smaller outside than it is sliced.
rules.why: Ten thin sleeves printed with classic walls came out with a 3.9 bore at 3.6: the pin did not enter. The reprint with the thin-wall generator took the pin and sat loose in its bearing. The third print was the fit ladder.
fix_order: Make the wall two lines or more.
Keep it as one line: thin-wall generator on that object, checked in the sliced path.
Take both diameters from a printed fit ladder (walls.one_line_ladder).
Owner waiver that names the ladder and the sizes that fitted.

rules.title: No sliver faces
rules.statement: No planar face of a printed part is a leftover narrower than {walls.min_face_width}: a sliver, a narrow ledge, the crescent left by an old hole, the land of a rib that is too thin. Old holes are filled before new ones are cut. Cuts and fills end on existing faces. Features never meet on an edge only: the body is one lump, and no edge joins more than two faces. A narrow face is judged by how it joins its neighbours, not by its width alone. One flat of a chamfer, a bevel or a faceted curve (a tooth flank) is no leftover: each of its long sides turns by at most {walls.strip_turn_max} deg, and the sides that turn by more than half of that turn the same way. The bridge steps of {overhang.bridge_step} between a counterbore and its hole are a print aid and no leftover. Narrow faces that touch are one finding. Equal places that repeat round one axis (the teeth of a wheel, a spline, a knurl: at least 12 places with the same faces and widths, on the steps of one even division of one circle) are one finding for the profile, with the count, the axis and one place; a place that differs keeps a row of its own. How thick the material is behind a face is not judged here: the wall check on the STL measures it (walls.min_material, walls.one_line). The check runs on every discovered part of every document, not on a typed list.
rules.why: A 1 mm groove ledge, 0.2 to 0.3 mm crescents of old insert holes and 0.5 mm slivers reached the slicer; the owner found them by eye. The check ran on a hand-typed list of five parts in whatever document was active. One part had 72 intended hits and no way to waive them, so the result was read by eye as "nothing new". On the first run over a whole assembly the width alone gave 2892 rows on ten parts, 2356 of them the tooth flanks of one pulley: a rule that counts every narrow face is read by nobody.
fix_order: Fill the old hole completely before the new one is cut.
End the cut or fill on an existing face; move it so that no strip is left.
Remove a ledge that has no function.
Two volumes that meet on an edge only: let them overlap, or move them apart.
An intended thin face that the check does not know as a strip or as bridge steps: owner waiver for that place; everything else reaches zero.
rules.note: The probe lists every planar face up to its width cap with the turn at each of its edges. A face whose edges the unit could not read is judged by its width alone, one row per face. Stored facts of an older unit, which read no edges at all, are not judged by width: one row says that the check did not run and the part is to be run again. The bridge steps are known from the holes of the census: a region of narrow faces between a counterbore and the narrower hole on its axis, treads that look out of the mouth and low walls tangent to the hole. A profile is told from the facts alone: the places are equal (the same number of faces, the same way they join, widths within 0.05 mm), there are at least 12 of them, all on one circle within 0.05 mm and each on a step of one even division of it. Both numbers are decided, not measured. The profile row is anchored on its axis and its context holds the count and one place, so a waiver covers the whole profile, expires when a place joins, leaves or changes, and never covers another defect of the part. Where the test is not met the places stay rows of their own.

rules.title: The size of a one-line wall comes from a fit ladder
rules.statement: A tube whose wall is one extrusion line prints smaller outside than it is sliced, and its bore is not the model's either. Both diameters come from a printed fit ladder: one row per dimension in steps of 0.05, the pieces told apart by height. The rows are not independent: the bore row is printed at the outer diameter that won the first row and is valid only near it. A size is measured only when the owner has named the piece that fits; until then it is decided.
rules.why: Sleeves with a one-line wall fitted the pin and sat loose in the bearing: sliced right, printed small outside. Ten more sleeves went to waste; then a ladder of 2.5 g and 18 minutes was printed.
fix_order: Print the ladder for the outer diameter first, then the bore row at the winning outer diameter.
Record the two winners together with the ladder they came from; the waiver on walls.one_line names them.

rules.title: Feature sizes follow the nozzle of the target project
rules.statement: Minimum feature sizes follow the nozzle ({target.nozzle}) and line width ({target.line_width}) of the project the part is placed in. No chamfer, slit, land or rib is narrower than one line. A thin feature is a whole number of lines or layers. A thin horizontal sheet has at least {walls.min_layers} layers. Small text has strokes at least one line wide. A part with features finer than the nozzle prints goes to a project with a finer nozzle; it is not left in the coarse one.
rules.why: Holders printed badly at a 0.62 line. Four labels were unreadable and were reprinted. Printed washers came out with an empty first layer. A tooth land of 0.3 mm was half a bead on a 0.6 nozzle: the belt did not seat on the printed pulley, and the part moved to a 0.4 project.
fix_order: Widen the feature to a whole number of lines or layers.
Move the part to a project with a finer nozzle and declare that target.
Buy the thin part in metal (a shim, a washer) instead of printing it.

rules.title: A load-carrying part is grown to its neighbour
rules.statement: A load-carrying part is grown to its real limiting neighbour instead of being sized to a minimum: where the space exists a structural wall is {walls.structural_target}; a wall in a load path is at least {walls.load_path_min}; no load path runs through a thin bridge. Clearance cuts follow the real envelope of the moving part. Thin open plates are closed into continuous walls with full-height ribs.
rules.why: Free space beside a two-screw strip stayed unused until the owner pointed at it. Thin walls against a gear unit were found by him in the slicer.
fix_order: Look for the real neighbour on each side before a wall is sized.
Count the screws again when a part grows: a bigger part can carry more of them.

rules.title: Geometry that lost its function is removed
rules.statement: Geometry that lost its function is removed in the pass that orphaned it, on printed parts too. A fill ends exactly on the intended surface: no dent, seam or witness mark. A dent or pocket shallower than {walls.leftover_depth} and a step lower than {walls.min_step} are leftovers, not features.
rules.why: Six dents 0.2 mm deep stayed visible to the owner as circles on a printed face.
fix_order: Fill the leftover flush with the surface it sits in.
Scan the body for shallow faces after every fill.
